name: Managed futures trend following (diversified time-series momentum)

origin.source_title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing (AQR white paper 2014; Journal of Portfolio Management 2017)

how_it_works.simple: If something has been going up, bet it keeps going up; if it has been going down, bet it keeps falling. Do this for many markets at once.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a surfer who does not guess where waves start but jumps on any wave already moving and steps off when it fades.
how_it_works.precise: For each futures or forward market, take a long position if its past excess return over a lookback is positive and a short if negative, sizing every position to the same ex ante volatility. Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen combine 1, 3 and 12 month lookbacks over 67 markets in four asset classes and scale the portfolio to 10% annual volatility. Returns are close to uncorrelated with stocks and bonds and tended to be positive in long equity bear markets.

rule: Each month, for each of N futures, compute the sign of the past 1, 3 and 12 month excess return; position = average of the three signs times (target risk / ex ante volatility of that market); scale the total book to 10% annual ex ante volatility; rebalance monthly.
data_needed: Continuous (rolled) futures or forward returns for equity indices, bonds, commodities and currencies, daily or monthly
Short-term interest rates for excess returns
economic_rationale: Investor underreaction followed by delayed overreaction, plus hedging flows, create return persistence at 1 to 12 months (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen 2014).
why_it_might_fail: Trend following loses in choppy markets and at sharp reversals; AQR's own TSMOM factor had a Sharpe ratio of about 0.38 from 2012 to mid 2026 versus about 1.4 up to 2009 (catalog computation from AQR data), and the SG Trend Index was down 9.3% in the first four months of 2025.

reported_results.market: 67 markets: equity indices, bonds, commodities, currencies
reported_results.notes: Net of simulated transaction costs and of a hypothetical 2% management and 20% performance fee; gross of fees the annualized return was 14.9%. Correlation to US equities 0.00. Transaction costs assumed 6 times 2012 levels before 1993.
Net of simulated costs and 2/20 fees; gross 11.3%. Correlation to US equities -0.30.

reported_results.source: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012), Time Series Momentum
reported_results.notes: Paper reports a Sharpe ratio greater than one (no exact figure in the passage read) and an alpha of about 1.58% per month versus market, SMB, HML and UMD; diversified portfolio annualized volatility about 12%.

Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. 12-month lookback, 1-month hold. The dataset does not state that costs are deducted, so treat as gross.

post_publication_evidence: After the 2012 Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen publication, the AQR TSMOM factor's Sharpe ratio fell to about 0.38 (2012 to 2026-05, catalog computation) from about 1.41 over 1985 to 2009. Societe Generale reports the SG Trend Index lost 4.9% in April 2025 and was down 9.3% year to date (https://content.sgmarkets.com/CTA_UPDATE_KEEPING_UP_WITH_THE_TRENDFOLLOWERS_2025). McLean and Pontiff (2016) find that across 97 published stock return predictors, portfolio returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication (https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.12365).

implementations.notes: Futures trading framework by Rob Carver; the provided rules folder includes ewmac.py (trend) and carry.py. Repo moved from robcarver17/pysystemtrade.

relevance.reason: Currency trend following is one of the four sleeves, so this is the closest well-documented template for an FX strategy that aims to diversify away from the S&P 500.
